info:
Kanji are not letters that represent sounds; they are meaning-based symbols. A single kanji usually represents a core concept (山 = mountain, 火 = fire), and many words are created by combining these concepts together. 火山 (fire + mountain=volcano).

Combining two kanji does not simply mean saying the two individual words together. Instead, the two kanji combine to create a new word with a related meaning. 山: Yama + 火: Hi = 火山 Kazan.

They can also be used similar to the way english uses root words with different endings (often hiragana).
